name: manual_e0ff7f
claim: PT memory catch-up: 5 substantive MiniGraph developments landed in orama-system's 2026-08-27-minigraph-final-reconciliation branch after lesson_4a711949b3ed and the GraphObservation supersession (c8e4d29b7f31) were recorded, and were never captured in PT memory until now. Final state as of commit d021d76b: (1) PerpetuaState.merge() had a genuine, verified shallow-copy leak -- Pydantic's model_copy() defaults to shallow, so nested mutable fields (scratchpad, messages, metadata, nodes_visited) absent from a delta were the same dict/list object shared between the old and new state; reproduced directly (mutating the new state's scratchpad in place corrupted the prior state through the shared reference) and fixed with model_copy(update=delta, deep=True), commit b002fc9d. (2) 01-kernel-spec.md's own §4a code sample was reconciled with the GraphObservation architecture c8e4d29b7f31 established only in prose -- _run() is now the sole scheduler yielding rich GraphObservation records (event + state + optional delta); aobserve() is the trusted in-process projection; asteps() is a thin sanitized GraphEvent projection over _run(), not a competing scheduler; the plugin fan-out sample was fixed to drain aobserve() and deliver the real delta instead of a hardcoded {} it previously passed to Checkpointer plugins, commit b5abb5b1. (3) The R2.4 regression-proof requirement in the observer-fanout addendum was strengthened to require both plugins record every event kind symmetrically (not an asymmetric subset) and an explicit no-plugin baseline run for state-parity comparison, commit 2e775b60. (4) MiniGraph.add_node()/add_edge() were made genuinely immutable -- each returns a new MiniGraph instance via structural sharing (only the changed dict is shallow-copied; the unchanged dict is shared by reference with the original, verified via identity check) rather than mutating self in place, resolving a direct conflict between an earlier "copy-on-write, mutation is fine" instruction and a later review demanding literal immutability by satisfying both simultaneously instead of picking a side, commit d021d76b. This closes a real footgun: a bare add_node() call with no reassignment now correctly leaves the original untouched instead of silently mutating it. (5) A real merge conflict during the immutable-builder edit (a separate commit landing on the same branch mid-session, touching the exact paragraph being rewritten) was resolved by saving changes as patches, resetting to the actual remote tip, and reapplying -- both the concurrent GraphSpec MUST-reject fix and the immutable-builder synthesis survived together, confirmed via direct verification rather than assumed.

decisions.notes: Direct question prompted actual verification, which found PT memory was genuinely stale relative to 5 real, pushed, CI-green orama developments -- closing that gap now rather than leaving it.
